scope: super_dome re-check after ART-B's round-24 fixes 1-8. Blender-only, provisional. Evidence art/dome/overview_250_day.png, overview_250_night.png (bloom pass), pilot_overview_day.png, pilot_overview_night.png, pilot_atrium_pool.png, pilot_atrium_night.png, pilot_gallery_L1.png, pilot_cutaway_L1.png. Rubric v5_rubrics.md 3.9.

round_24_fixes_checked.1 night facade: landed: windows now vary (warm amber, cream, cool blue, about a quarter dark), light strips on the gallery slabs, neon signs CLOTHING / ELECTRONICS / GIFTS and a lit billboard on the L1 outer face. At 250 m I count 4-5 light colours. Still reads more 'lit office ring' than 'city': the upper three floors are an even grid of equal windows, and the neon is only on one low band facing the camera.
round_24_fixes_checked.2 frame thinner and metal: landed: graphite struts about half the old width, small warm node lights. The day view now reads glass first.
round_24_fixes_checked.3 glass reflection: partly: the glass has a faint tint and a highlight rim, but no sky reflection or fresnel gradient is visible; the dome still reads as clear film at 250 m by day.
round_24_fixes_checked.4 signs: landed: CREDIT, RESTAURANT, CAFE and CLINIC read; HOTEL is still clipped at its left edge by the tree ('OTEL' reads as 'HOTEL' only in part), and the barber sign in the gallery view is cut by a column ('AR ER').
round_24_fixes_checked.5 pool glow: landed: cyan rim-lit pool, warm plaza lamps and string lights at night (pilot_atrium_night.png); from the 250 m night view the atrium is the bright heart.
round_24_fixes_checked.6 venues filled: partly: the cutaway shows more (clothing racks and mannequins, grocery shelf rows, electronics counters, hotel sofas); inside the gallery view the cafe goods are plain coloured boxes on tables and the wall screens are flat cyan rectangles.
round_24_fixes_checked.7 props: landed: slatted benches with graphite frames; palms and trees now match the colony plant family (palms are a new but fitting choice for a resort).
round_24_fixes_checked.8 pool water: partly: a darker edge and a rim light, no tile or lane pattern; the surface is still a flat light blue by day.

gap_to_paul_aim.night_overview_250m: Close to the mark. It is now the brightest object in the scene, with a glowing atrium, varied windows and neon at street level. What keeps it from glittering: the glass shell itself is almost invisible at night (no rim glow, no reflections of the city lights), and the lights are too regular on L3-L5. Estimate 0.72 against the aim (0.80 = glitters).
gap_to_paul_aim.day_overview_250m: Reads as a domed city; the glass needs a sky reflection to feel like glass. Estimate 0.70.
gap_to_paul_aim.inside: The atrium at night is the best image of the dome: resort mood, pool glow, neon signs, warm lamps. The gallery still needs goods with detail. Estimate 0.74.

fixes.fix: Break the grid on L3-L5: per unit, vary window size (2 widths), add small balconies or planter boxes on every third unit, and let some units show a TV-blue flicker or a coloured lamp; add 2-3 more neon or sign bands at L2 around the full ring (not only the camera side).

Night glass: a faint emissive rim along the dome edge and at the crown ring, plus the city lights reflected in the glass panes (in game: screen-space or a cheap reflection probe tinted warm), so the shell itself glitters.
Day glass: sky reflection with fresnel (25-40% at grazing angles). This was fix 3 and is still open.
Signs: keep HOTEL and BARBER plates clear of trees and columns from the atrium and gallery views (move the plate, or the tree 1.5 m).
Venue goods: replace plain boxes with type props (cakes and cups on the cafe counter, boxed goods with labels, a menu board); give the wall screens content (a menu, an advert) instead of flat cyan.
Pool: a tile or lane pattern and a darker deep end so it reads as water by day.
In-game: the 250 m night shot with the game's glow, the draw-call count, and glass sorting against the ring. This decides the final score.

notes: PASS 0.74 (was 0.68), provisional. 5 of 8 fixes fully landed, 3 partly (glass reflection, venue goods, pool water).

Seen in passing: in the gallery view a customer stands inside the table top (hips through the table edge). The people are placeholders, but RENDER's seat and stand anchors must keep bodies clear of the cafe tables.
